response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM film_actor GROUP BY film_id), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS m FROM c), s1 AS (SELECT c.film_id, c.n, c.n - a1.m AS e1 FROM c, a1 WHERE c.n > a1.m), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS m FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.film_id, s1.n, s1.e1, s1.n - a2.m AS e2 FROM s1, a2 WHERE s1.n > a2.m) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_actor_count, AVG(e1) AS avg_excess_over_first, AVG(e2) AS avg_excess_over_second FROM s2

assumptions.assumption: Actor count per film is the number of film_actor rows (COUNT(*)); the primary key (actor_id, film_id) makes these distinct actors.
If no films remain, the query returns one row with NULL values (SUM and AVG over an empty set), which matches 'keep no films' for a missing average.
